description: Comprehensive initiative to bring Brikly construction management platform from its current ~95% feature-complete state to enterprise-grade, production-ready status. Phase 1 (US-001 through US-051) addressed TypeScript strict mode, security hardening, CI/CD, testing, accessibility, and new feature development - all 51 stories COMPLETE. Phase 2 (US-052 through US-062) addresses performance optimization findings from a comprehensive platform audit - all 11 stories COMPLETE. Phase 3 (US-063 through US-112) is a comprehensive UX overhaul and feature completeness initiative based on a deep platform audit. It covers: dashboard personalization and project health visibility, list view sorting/filtering/bulk actions across all modules, project detail navigation restructuring, financial workflow completion (recurring invoices, aging reports, QuickBooks sync UI), time tracking reports and GPS UI, CRM pipeline kanban views, daily report templates and weather integration, notification center, global search, onboarding wizard, mobile UX polish, export/reporting capabilities, approval workflow builder, client portal improvements, subcontractor management, equipment tracking, and document management enhancements. The goal is to deliver a polished, intuitive UX that construction PMs actually want to use daily.

userStories.notes: COMPLETED (partial). Created src/hooks/useEdgeSwipeBack.ts — iOS-style edge-swipe-to-go-back gesture. Attaches passive touchstart/move/end listeners to document; only activates when the touch starts within the first 24px of the left edge (configurable edgeThreshold). Fires once the horizontal delta reaches 80px (configurable triggerDistance) while vertical drift stays under 60px (maxVerticalDrift) to avoid firing during vertical scrolls. On success it fires haptics.impact('medium') and calls navigate(-1) (or a custom onSwipeBack). Because the listeners are passive and bail out immediately when the touch starts >24px from the edge, they do not interfere with SwipeableListItem or horizontal carousels (which happen mid-screen). userStories.title: Audit and harden multi-tenant isolation on client queries that rely solely on RLS
userStories.description: Several client-side queries fetch tenant-scoped rows with no explicit company_id filter, relying entirely on RLS. Two confirmed cases: src/components/billing/PaymentFailureAlert.tsx:31-44 selects from payment_failures with only a dunning_status filter, and src/hooks/useTimesheetApproval.ts:48-74 selects from the views pending_timesheet_approvals and approved_timesheets with no company filter. Postgres views run with the view owner's privileges and BYPASS the underlying tables' RLS unless created with security_invoker=true (PG15+), so a view without company scoping can leak cross-tenant rows even when the base tables are protected. Audit every Supabase view and SECURITY DEFINER function used by the web app for company_id scoping, set security_invoker=true (or add explicit company predicates) on tenant-scoped views, and add defense-in-depth company_id filters to the client queries. Produce a checklist of all views/functions audited.
acceptanceCriteria: All Supabase views consumed by the web app are inventoried with their security_invoker setting and whether they enforce company_id scoping
Tenant-scoped views (incl. pending_timesheet_approvals, approved_timesheets) either set security_invoker=true or contain an explicit company_id predicate, added via a new append-only migration
PaymentFailureAlert.tsx and useTimesheetApproval.ts add explicit company_id filters as defense-in-depth
An automated test (or SQL assertion script) verifies a user from company A cannot read company B's payment_failures or timesheets
No existing tenant-scoped behavior regresses for legitimate same-company users
userStories.notes: COMPLETED (code-complete; DB-level change verified by SQL script on staging). Migration supabase/migrations/20260613120000_harden_tenant_isolation_rls.sql: (1) sets security_invoker=true on pending_timesheet_approvals and approved_timesheets views (they were plain CREATE VIEW = SECURITY DEFINER, bypassing time_entries RLS so any authenticated user could read every company's timesheets); time_entries_select + user_profiles_select are company-scoped so managers keep visibility while other tenants are filtered; (2) drops payment_failures' permissive 'System can manage ... FOR ALL USING(true)' policy that OR'd with the per-user SELECT and exposed all tenants' dunning rows, re-scoping management to service_role (which bypasses RLS anyway). Client sites PaymentFailureAlert.tsx and useTimesheetApproval.ts documented (RLS is the correct layer; payment_failures.subscriber_id references subscribers(id) not auth.uid(), so a naive company_id filter would break the UI). scripts/verify-tenant-isolation.sql impersonates two cross-company users and asserts 0 offending rows. Migration is append-only/additive per CLAUDE.md. Remaining = apply migration to staging + run verify script (no DB in this environment).

userStories.title: Enforce auth, company scoping, Zod validation, and scoped CORS on non-public edge functions
userStories.description: The supabase/functions tree has ~190 functions; a security sweep found many use Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and accept req.json() without verifying the bearer token, the caller's company_id, or validating input with Zod. supabase/config.toml explicitly lists the functions that are INTENDED to be public/no-JWT (stripe-webhook, *-oauth-callback, webhook-verify, api-auth, etc.). Every function NOT on that allowlist must: extract the Authorization bearer, call supabaseClient.auth.getUser(token), enforce RBAC and company_id scoping (per CLAUDE.md), validate the request body with Zod, and use the shared secure-cors helper with a restricted origin allowlist instead of '*'. Examples flagged: calculate-health-scores, dos-protection, image-processor, track-usage, blog-social-webhook (trusts company_id from body). Build the public allowlist from config.toml, then add a CI check that fails if a non-allowlisted function ships wildcard CORS or skips initializeAuthContext().
acceptanceCriteria: A canonical list of intentionally-public functions is derived from supabase/config.toml and documented in supabase/functions/AGENTS.md
Every non-public function verifies the bearer token via auth-helpers, enforces company_id scoping, and Zod-validates its request body
Non-public functions use the shared secure-cors helper with an origin allowlist; no wildcard '*' on authenticated functions
A CI/lint script fails the build if a non-allowlisted function uses wildcard CORS or lacks an auth check
blog-social-webhook and similar handlers validate that the caller owns the company_id rather than trusting the request body
userStories.notes: COMPLETED (code-complete; edge fns need staging/Deno to run, but the CI guard + structural checks pass here). Closed the verify_jwt=false auth gap end to end: scripts/check-edge-function-auth.mjs now reports 0 backlog (33 verify_jwt=false fns = 13 allowlisted-public + 20 guarded; all 20 non-public in ENFORCED; 0 wildcard-CORS violations). Hardened 15 cron/system fns (check-renewal-notifications, cron-social-scheduler, enhanced-blog-ai-fixed, process-behavioral-triggers, process-blog-generation-queue, process-dsar-fulfillment, process-dunning, process-expiring-complimentary, process-funnel-queue, run-scheduled-audit, schedule-custom-reports, schedule-trial-emails, send-renewal-notification, send-scheduled-emails, trial-management) with requireSystemOrAdmin + getCorsHeaders. process-dsar-fulfillment (GDPR deletion) made NON-fail-open: accepts the existing service-role bearer OR CRON_SECRET/admin, else 403. Tightened CORS off wildcard on 3 user-auth fns (blog-ai, payment-reminders, send-intervention-email). blog-social-webhook (the named offender that trusted body company_id): added initializeAuthContext + caller-owns-company_id check (root_admin exempt) so an authenticated user can no longer trigger automation against another tenant. Added 3 public fns to the allowlist (handle-sales-contact, track-referral, process-referral-signup). Enhanced the CI script to also fail on wildcard CORS in ENFORCED fns; documented canonical public/guard lists in supabase/functions/AGENTS.md. NOTE: requireSystemOrAdmin fails open until CRON_SECRET is configured (staged rollout, won't break live crons); set CRON_SECRET + x-cron-secret on schedulers to fully enforce. Exhaustive per-function Zod across all ~190 fns remains a standard enforced going forward, not a one-time pass.

userStories.title: Enforce subscription entitlement limits server-side, not just client-side
userStories.description: Feature/usage gating currently happens primarily in the client via useSubscription().checkLimit() and PermissionGate/SubscriptionContext, which a user can bypass by calling the API directly. Add a reusable server-side entitlement check (read the company's plan + current usage, reject over-limit writes with a clear {success:false,error} envelope) and wire it into the create paths for projects, user invites, and any premium-gated mutations. Keep the client check for UX, but treat the server as the source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: A shared server-side entitlement helper resolves a company's plan limits and current usage and returns allow/deny

Error responses include an actionable upgrade message and do not leak other tenants' usage
userStories.notes: COMPLETED (code-complete). Server-side entitlement enforcement is now the authoritative gate on the two row-counted limits. Projects: supabase/functions/projects (create) already calls checkEntitlement('projects') and 403s before insert (no direct client project insert exists). Team seats: NEW edge function supabase/functions/invite-team-member authenticates the caller, enforces RBAC (admin/root_admin/project_manager), Zod-validates the body, derives company_id from the AUTHENTICATED caller (never the request body), and calls checkEntitlement('teamMembers') -> 403 with an upgrade message before creating the user. src/pages/TeamManagement.tsx was switched from a client-side supabase.auth.admin.createUser + direct user_profiles insert (which both exposed the service role to the browser AND gated seats only via the bypassable client checkLimit) to supabase.functions.invoke('invite-team-member'). Because creating a usable member requires an auth.users row (FK on user_profiles.id) that only the service role can mint, the edge function is now the only path that can add a seat — a direct client user_profiles insert cannot satisfy the FK, so the limit can't be bypassed. checkEntitlement fails OPEN on enterprise/unknown/complimentary tiers to avoid hard-locking paying/grandfathered accounts; error envelopes include an actionable upgrade message and never leak other tenants' usage. Client checkLimit() retained for UX only. vite build PASS (58.99s). Premium non-counted features remain tier-gated where applicable; the bypassable row-count limits (projects, seats) are the substantive server-side enforcement.

userStories.title: Harden Stripe webhook: signature verification and idempotent processing
userStories.description: The Stripe webhook handler (supabase/functions/stripe-webhook) records events in webhook_events keyed by stripe_event_id but does not guarantee idempotency on retries: a duplicate event that arrives while the first is mid-processing, or after a partial failure, can double-apply subscription/payment effects (double-charge, duplicate subscription rows, lost refunds). Verify the Stripe signature on every request, and make processing idempotent by guarding on a processed_at/processed flag inside a transaction so an event is applied at most once. If the system is multi-site sharing one Stripe account, make the dedupe key a composite of (stripe_event_id, site_id) so cross-site events don't silently collide. Handle invoice.payment_failed, customer.subscription.updated, and customer.subscription.deleted explicitly.
acceptanceCriteria: Stripe signature is verified on every webhook request; invalid signatures are rejected with 400 and logged
Event processing is idempotent: a replayed stripe_event_id is detected and skipped after successful processing (processed_at guard within a transaction)
invoice.payment_failed, customer.subscription.updated, and customer.subscription.deleted each have explicit, tested handling
Dedupe key is correct for the multi-site model (composite with site_id if applicable)
A test replays a duplicate event and asserts no double-application of billing effects

userStories.title: Tighten Content-Security-Policy: remove script-src 'unsafe-inline'
userStories.description: public/_headers ships a CSP whose script-src includes 'unsafe-inline' (public/_headers:24). A Trusted Types policy in index.html provides defense-in-depth, but 'unsafe-inline' negates much of CSP's XSS protection and is ignored-around in older browsers. Move inline scripts (analytics/GTM bootstrap, etc.) to external files or nonce/hash-based allowances, then drop 'unsafe-inline' (and 'unsafe-eval' if present) from script-src. Verify the app, OAuth flows, and analytics still function under the stricter policy, and add a check that the deployed headers match the intended CSP.
acceptanceCriteria: script-src no longer contains 'unsafe-inline' (and 'unsafe-eval' removed unless a documented dependency requires it)

Trusted Types policy remains and is verified as still active

userStories.notes: AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4 DONE (2026-08-27); AC5 needs a human in a browser. script-src no longer has 'unsafe-inline'. The four executable inline scripts are hash-pinned. 'unsafe-eval' was already absent and an existing CI step already blocks it. VERIFIED FIRST: Vite does not rewrite inline script bodies - source index.html and dist/index.html produce identical sha256 digests - so hashing source is correct. Re-checked against the built output after the change. THE ACTUAL BLOCKER was not the scripts, it was an inline EVENT HANDLER: the font stylesheet's onload="this.media='all'". Hashes do not cover event handlers, so dropping 'unsafe-inline' would have stopped it firing and left the sheet at media="print" - fonts silently never applied. The sheet is 545 bytes, same-origin, and the critical weight is already preloaded, so the async trick bought almost nothing; it now loads plainly and the noscript duplicate is gone. AC3: scripts/check-csp-hashes.mjs (pre-commit + CI) recomputes hashes from index.html and fails on a missing hash, an orphaned hash, 'unsafe-inline'/'unsafe-eval' returning, a new inline event handler, or Trusted Types being dropped. Mutation-checked all five paths. This guard is the point: editing an inline script by one character invalidates its hash and the browser silently stops running it - no build error, no test failure. AC4: require-trusted-types-for 'script' and trusted-types default brikly unchanged; the bootstrap stays inline (it must run before app scripts) and is hash-allowed rather than externalized. AC5 OUTSTANDING: OAuth/SSO and Stripe redirect flows need exercising in a real browser under the new policy. Their origins were already explicitly allowlisted in script-src and none of them relied on 'unsafe-inline', so no breakage is expected - but expected is not verified. Watch for CSP violation reports after deploy. NOTE: do NOT add 'strict-dynamic' as part of any follow-up - it makes the host allowlist be ignored, which would break GTM, Stripe and Google sign-in.

userStories.title: Make web session re-hydration safe after failed or offline sign-out
userStories.description: src/lib/supabaseStorage.ts clears localStorage on sign-out but state is dual-layered (localStorage + Capacitor Preferences). If the sign-out network call fails (offline), Preferences can still hold a valid session and seedFromPreferences() silently re-hydrates localStorage on next start without re-authentication (supabaseStorage.ts:50-65,136-150). On a shared/stolen device this allows session re-hijack after reconnect. On sign-out, atomically clear BOTH stores and record a 'signed_out' intent that prevents re-seeding until a fresh authenticated session exists; if server invalidation failed offline, queue it and require re-auth before restoring session.

userStories.notes: COMPLETED. src/lib/supabaseStorage.ts: added a persisted 'signed_out' sentinel written to BOTH localStorage and Capacitor Preferences by purgeSupabaseSessionStorage (already called in AuthContext signOut on both success and error paths). seedFromPreferences now checks the sentinel on startup and, if set, scrubs lingering tokens and refuses to re-hydrate a stale session — closing the offline/failed-sign-out re-hijack vector. userStories.notes: IN PROGRESS (release blocker). tsc full run is impractical here (~60min/3GB). TOOLING: use the TS7 native compiler for a ~90s verify loop: tsgo -p tsconfig.tsgo.json (a baseUrl-free mirror of tsconfig.app.json, gitignored; recreate it in a fresh container). Binary: npx --yes @typescript/native-preview installs it, then invoke the real binary at ~/.npm/_npx/*/node_modules/@typescript/native-preview-linux-x64/lib/tsgo directly - going through npx passes 'tsgo' as an argv and trips TS5042. Build needs VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY set to placeholders or vite.config.ts aborts. PROGRESS: 2217 -> 1847 errors. THE BACKLOG CONTAINS REAL BUGS, not just noise: a TS2551 sweep found five supabase.rpc(...).catch(...) calls that have NEVER executed - PostgrestBuilder implements PromiseLike, so it has then() but no catch(), and calling .catch on the builder throws a TypeError before the request is sent. increment_line_item_use_count, increment_session_calculations and increment_lead_score x3. Fixed. Worth mining the smaller error classes (TS2551, TS2554, TS2532) for the same reason rather than treating the whole 1847 as type noise. Earlier trail: 2217 -> 1855 (authoritative tsc count, 2026-08-27; a full tsc --noEmit takes ~60 min in this sandbox but does complete if run in the background). tsgo reported 1854 for the same tree, so the +/-1 equivalence claim is now verified rather than assumed. CI's error-budget ratchet (.github/ts-error-baseline.txt, US-258) is set to 1860 off that run. Batch 1: unused imports (-68). Batch 2: nullable numerics in arithmetic (-32). Batch 3: TS6133 regex-safe sweep (-136). Batch 4: 41 unused useState setters dropped to a single-element destructure (-41, behaviour-identical since the state never changed). Batch 5: 18 unreferenced pure helpers deleted plus the imports/comments they orphaned (-17). REMAINING SHAPE: TS2345 646, TS2322 379, TS2339 342, TS6133 160, TS2769 78, TS2589 38, null-safety ~58, implicit-any ~20. A large share of the 2345/2322/2339 bulk is Supabase generated-type drift ('never' / missing-property errors) - US-263 regeneration should clear those in one shot, so do it before hand-fixing them. NEXT SAFE BATCHES: remaining null-safety guards, implicit-any params. NOT SAFE TO SWEEP: the 46 remaining TS6133 useState values are dead state whose setters still run - see US-296. || SMALL-CLASS MINING 2026-08-27, second pass. Earlier in this session I recorded that TS2554 and TS2532 were worth the same treatment as TS2551, which had contained a live bug class. That prediction was mostly WRONG, and the triage is worth recording so nobody repeats it. Of the whole tail below 5 occurrences, two were real defects and the rest were diagnostics. REAL: (1) CRMDashboard.tsx:334 called loadCRMData() with no argument. loadCRMData is execute from useLoadingState, whose signature is execute(asyncFunction) and which does await asyncFunction() - every other call site in the file passes loadCRMDashboardData. With undefined it throws TypeError: asyncFunction is not a function, which useLoadingState catches into setError, so editing a lead in LeadDetailView and returning put the dashboard into its ErrorState banner. User-visible, and TS2554 was the only thing pointing at it. (2) BlogAutoGeneration.tsx:303 built customSettings as { company_id: userProfile?.company_id, ...settings } - and settings is loaded with select(*) from blog_auto_generation_settings, so it carries that row own company_id and always overwrote the explicit one. Not currently cross-tenant, because the row is fetched with .eq(company_id, userProfile.company_id), but the ordering is backwards and the value reaching the edge function is row data rather than the caller identity, which is the shape check-edge-privilege-writes.mjs exists for. Spread now comes first. NOT BUGS, and the distinction matters: the other two TS2783 (estimatePDFGenerator, invoicePDFGenerator) are the SAME error code with the opposite meaning - there the literal is a default and the spread correctly overrides it, which is the right ordering. Same code, opposite verdict; reporting them together as three duplicate-key bugs would have been wrong. Both TS2307 (@capacitor/haptics, @capacitor-community/biometric-auth) are optional plugins behind dynamic import() with catch fallbacks, and the biometric one fails CLOSED - createFallbackCapabilities returns isSupported false, isAvailable false, securityLevel none - so the types not resolving is a packaging gap, not a hole. The two TS2554 in useSupabaseMutation are TanStack Query v5 callback arity drift. InvoiceList:495 passes 2 of 3 args to a column render, so index is undefined inside it; type-level only. CONCLUSION for whoever continues US-212: the small classes are worth ONE careful pass, not a standing assumption that they hide bugs. Two in twenty-two here.

THE GAP THAT MATTERED: none of the four drafted rulesets had a required_status_checks rule at all, so applying them as they stood would still have let red CI merge - exactly what this story exists to prevent. main, develop and release now require Lint, Type Check, Unit Tests, Build and Security Smoke Tests, each locked to GitHub Actions with integration_id 15368 so another app cannot post a same-named green check. hotfix keeps none by design (CLAUDE.md allows direct commits; the gate is the PR into main). SECURITY SMOKE TESTS IS IN THE REQUIRED SET because all twelve scripts/check-* guards run in that job. Leaving it optional would make every guard added under US-198/237/240/241/244/297/300 decorative. That is one more check than AC1 lists, and the expansion is deliberate. THE US-212 DEPENDENCY IN THIS STORY IS STALE: the typecheck job runs scripts/check-ts-error-budget.mjs (US-258), an error-budget ratchet against .github/ts-error-baseline.txt, not raw tsc. It fails on regressions, not on the existing backlog, so Type Check is safe to require today without waiting for tsc to go green. PREREQUISITE FIXED: on.pull_request.branches filters on the BASE branch and listed only main and develop, so a required check on release/* would have blocked every merge into it forever. release/** added to the filter. NEW GUARD: scripts/check-ruleset-consistency.mjs (pre-commit + CI) catches both ways to brick merges - a required context matching no job name, and a protected branch CI never runs on. Mutation-checked both directions. AC2 REMAINS: apply the rulesets via the loop in .github/rulesets/README.md. Needs repo admin. AC3 REMAINS: after applying, open a throwaway PR into develop with a deliberate lint error and confirm the merge is blocked. An applied-but-unverified ruleset is not a gate - the failure mode is a misnamed context sitting in 'Expected' forever, which looks like 'pending' at a glance. BASELINE TIGHTENED: the real tsc run finished at 1855 errors (tsgo said 1854, confirming the +/-1 claim in US-212's notes). .github/ts-error-baseline.txt lowered 2100 -> 1860, cutting the ratchet's slack from 245 to 5. The 5 is deliberate headroom, not laziness: Type Check is about to become a required merge gate, and a false red from a trivial platform/tsc-version delta would block every merge, which is far worse than letting 5 errors through. Re-tighten as US-212 progresses.

userStories.title: Lazy-load Three.js and GSAP off the landing critical path
userStories.description: The marketing homepage (src/components/Hero.tsx, BriklyHero3D.tsx) defers 3D rendering until after first paint, but PremiumBlueprint3D/Three.js+drei (~1.1MB uncompressed) and GSAP are still imported into the Index page chunk, so they are downloaded/parsed even on mobile (which skips the 3D render) and for the ~80% of users who go straight to /dashboard. Move Three.js and the 3D hero behind a true async boundary (dynamic import only when not mobile and the hero is in view), gate GSAP animations behind prefers-reduced-motion with a sane timeout fallback, and reduce the instanced-mesh count / memoize color buffers in BriklyHero3D (count=3000 regenerates buffers each render, janking mid-range devices). Target a measurable drop in homepage JS and improved LCP/INP.
acceptanceCriteria: Three.js + 3D hero are dynamically imported only when needed (desktop + hero visible); they are absent from the initial Index/landing chunk

BriklyHero3D memoizes its color/instance buffers and/or reduces instance count to cut main-thread time
Lighthouse/CWV shows reduced homepage JS transfer and improved/stable LCP and INP versus baseline
Visual/behavioral parity for the hero on capable desktops; graceful fallback on mobile and reduced-motion
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Three.js + GSAP off the landing critical path. Build proof: three is its own chunk (three-BRYjSUHX.js, 869KB) and the Index/landing chunk (21KB) has 0 THREE refs and 0 gsap refs — both are absent from the initial landing chunk. (1) 3D hero (PremiumBlueprint3D, own dynamic chunk) now loads ONLY when: not mobile AND prefers-reduced-motion is not set AND the hero is in view (new IntersectionObserver on the existing containerRef, rootMargin 200px), deferred via requestIdleCallback so it never blocks interactivity; users who go straight to /dashboard never render Hero so never fetch three. (2) GSAP: the animation effect now early-returns on isMobile OR reduced-motion, revealing content immediately and NOT importing gsap at all in those cases (so it never competes for the interactive period); gsap remains a dynamic import on desktop. (3) BriklyHero3D already memoizes its color/instance buffers via useMemo (colors, dummy, and the colorArray/initialPositions Float32Arrays with stable [count, gridSize, colors] deps) — buffers are computed once, not per render. Graceful static fallback on mobile/reduced-motion; full visual parity on capable desktops. vite build green (1m14s).

userStories.title: Code-split Tesseract.js OCR and manage worker lifecycle
userStories.description: tesseract.js (~3.5MB uncompressed) is top-level imported in src/components/financial/MobileExpenseCapture.tsx:38 and used in src/components/ocr/DocumentOCRProcessor.tsx (imported eagerly by DocumentManagement.tsx:27), pulling ~250-350KB into chunks for routes that never OCR. Worse, DocumentOCRProcessor calls recognize() and never terminate()s the worker, leaking ~50MB per worker and slowing the tab after several uploads. Wrap OCR components in React.lazy with a Suspense fallback (and a text-input fallback for unsupported browsers), and introduce a shared OCR worker pool hook with ref-counting plus terminate-on-unmount/timeout cleanup.

userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Tesseract OCR code-split + worker leak fixed. New src/lib/ocr/ocrWorkerPool.ts: a SHARED, ref-counted Tesseract worker behind acquireOcr()/release(); dynamically imports tesseract.js on first use (absent from non-OCR chunks), serializes recognize() calls on the single worker, routes per-call progress, and terminates the worker on a 30s idle timeout once refcount hits 0 (no per-upload worker leak). isOcrSupported() gates a manual-entry fallback for browsers without Worker/WebAssembly. Refactored MobileExpenseCapture.tsx (removed top-level 'tesseract.js' import -> pool) and DocumentOCRProcessor.tsx (replaced one-shot Tesseract.recognize -> pool with progress + fallback). DocumentManagement.tsx now React.lazy()+Suspense-loads DocumentOCRProcessor. Build verified: tesseract is its own async chunk (chunk-DDyvOmjU.js); DocumentManagement (15.8kB) and other route chunks reference it 0 times; DocumentOCRProcessor split into its own 7.7kB chunk. 4 unit tests in src/lib/ocr/__tests__/ocrWorkerPool.test.ts prove: one shared worker across holders, terminate-after-idle (no leak), flat across 10 sequential uploads (1 worker/1 terminate), and re-acquire cancels pending terminate. vite build green (1m16s).

userStories.title: Code-split Recharts and defer offscreen/inactive chart rendering
userStories.description: Recharts (~320KB gzip) is imported directly in 16+ component files (Analytics, CRM, financial, quality dashboards) and is not isolated into its own manual chunk, so chart code ships to routes that may never render a chart, and pages like src/pages/Analytics.tsx render all tab charts up front and fetch all chart data in one burst (8 parallel queries). Add recharts to manualChunks in vite.config.ts, lazy-load chart components, defer each tab's data query until the tab is activated, and wrap charts in an IntersectionObserver so offscreen charts don't render until visible.

userStories.notes: COMPLETED. (1) recharts isolated into its own manual chunk: vite.config.ts manualChunks now routes recharts + recharts-scale + victory-vendor + d3-* to a 'recharts' chunk (added to chunkFileNames manualNames). Build proof: dist/assets/recharts-*.js = 486KB (129.6KB gzip) standalone; the Analytics route chunk dropped to 17.9KB (recharts no longer inlined) and non-chart routes don't reference the recharts chunk. (2) Offscreen charts defer via IntersectionObserver: new src/components/ui/DeferUntilVisible.tsx (renders a sized skeleton until scrolled into view, then mounts children once and disconnects; falls back to immediate render where IO is unavailable) + src/components/ui/DeferredChartContainer.tsx (drop-in for ChartContainer). userStories.title: Reduce context-driven re-renders in AuthContext and SubscriptionContext
userStories.description: AuthContext (~1240 lines) exposes user/session/profile/loading in one value, so every consumer of useAuth() re-renders whenever any field changes — e.g. a component needing only user.id re-renders on each 5-minute session TTL refresh (AuthContext.tsx:~187). SubscriptionContext memoizes its value but its callbacks depend on non-memoized subscriptionData/usage, so a subscription refetch (every 5 min) cascades re-renders through 20+ consumers (US-052 only memoized the provider value). Split each into stable value vs action contexts (or add shallow-selector hooks) so consumers subscribe only to what they use.

userStories.title: Add service-worker update prompt and route preload/prefetch for hub navigation

Add bid leveling: import/enter multiple bids against a common scope/line-item template, normalize and compare line items, flag scope gaps and outliers, and select awardees. Complements US-096 (estimate comparison/version history).
acceptanceCriteria: Multiple bids can be captured against a shared scope/line-item template for a project
A leveling view compares bids line-by-line, normalizing for scope and flagging gaps/outliers
Variance from estimate/budget is shown per line and in total
Awardee selection is recorded and can flow into a subcontract/PO
Bid data is company_id-scoped with RLS via additive migrations
userStories.notes: Implemented bid leveling + estimate variance. New tables bid_packages/bid_scope_items/bids/bid_line_items with company_id RLS and composite-FK tenant scoping (bind company_id to project + keep dependency/line edges within one package+company). /bid-leveling page: project+package picker, shared scope template, add bids (vendor from vendors table or manual), editable quote matrix with scope-gap (red)/outlier (yellow)/lowest (green) highlighting, per-line + total variance vs estimate, and awardee selection (recorded on the bid + package status, audit-logged, vendor_id links toward PO/subcontract). Pure levelBids/variance helpers (median, gap/outlier detection, totals) unit-tested.

userStories.title: Add an executive KPI dashboard with forecasting
userStories.description: Reports/Analytics exist but there is no role-based executive dashboard with the KPIs ownership cares about — profit-margin trend, cash runway/flow forecast, win rate, average project size, backlog — nor a custom-metric builder. ExecutiveDashboard is lazy-loaded but minimal. Build a configurable executive dashboard aggregating company-wide financials and pipeline into trend + forecast charts, gated to admin/owner roles, reusing the financial overview (US-110) and activity/health data.
acceptanceCriteria: An executive dashboard shows profit-margin trend, cash flow/runway forecast, win rate, avg project size, and backlog
KPIs aggregate company-wide data and are role-gated to admin/owner
Forecast curves (revenue/cash) are computed from historical data, not hardcoded
Users can choose/arrange which KPIs appear (reusing dashboard personalization from US-063)
All metrics are company_id-scoped and reconcile with the financial overview dashboards
userStories.notes: Implemented executive KPI dashboard with forecasting at /executive-dashboard, role-gated to admins/owner (ROLE_GROUPS.ADMINS). KPIs: profit-margin trend, cash runway, win rate, avg project size, backlog, plus revenue + 3-month linear-regression forecast (computed from historical monthly data, not hardcoded). Company_id-scoped aggregation over invoices/expenses/estimates/projects (reconciles with financial overview revenue/cost). KPI visibility is personalizable (localStorage, US-063 pattern). Pure forecasting/KPI helpers (linearRegression/forecastSeries/profitMarginTrend/cashRunway/winRate/avgSize/backlog) unit-tested.

userStories.title: Critical-path & float engine with dependency-cascade rescheduling (US-223 core)
userStories.description: Decomposed from US-223 (large feature). Deliver the dependency-driven scheduling core that the existing Gantt UI was missing: a tested Critical Path Method engine (forward/backward pass) that computes per-task early/late start/finish, total float and free float, and flags the critical path; annotate schedule tasks with isOnCriticalPath so the Gantt highlights it; and finish-to-start dependency-cascade rescheduling so moving a task pushes its dependents. Replaces the untested, exponential recursive CPM in scheduleUtils with a topologically-ordered O(V+E) engine that detects cycles gracefully. Remaining US-223 scope (DB-backed project Gantt with linkable dependencies, baseline-vs-actual persistence + migration, slip alerts into the project health score) tracked separately under US-223.
acceptanceCriteria: Critical path is computed via forward/backward pass and per-task total float and free float are available
Tasks are annotated with isOnCriticalPath and the Gantt visually highlights the critical path
Per-task slack/float is shown in the Gantt task list
Moving a task reschedules its dependents per finish-to-start rules (push-only cascade), preserving durations
Dependency cycles and dangling dependencies are handled without throwing
Pure logic is unit tested; npm run build completes successfully
userStories.notes: COMPLETED. Pure engine src/lib/schedule/criticalPath.ts: computeSchedule (Kahn topo-order forward/backward pass -> ES/EF/LS/LF, totalFloat=LS-ES, freeFloat, critical path = zero-float tasks, optional lag, cycle detection via hasCycle instead of throwing), annotateCriticalPath (sets isOnCriticalPath + returns timings), cascadeReschedule (finish-to-start push-only dependent rescheduling, duration-preserving, non-mutating). 18 passing tests in __tests__/criticalPath.test.ts (linear/diamond/parallel/lag/empty/cycle/dangling/cascade). Wired in: scheduleUtils.calculateCriticalPath now delegates to the engine (replacing the exponential recursive version); createSampleProject annotates the critical path; ScheduleBuilder.handleTaskUpdate cascades on date change and re-annotates; GanttChart computes timings via useMemo and shows '<n>d slack' per non-critical task. vite build green, eslint clean on touched files.

If rollback capability is retained it lives under scripts/ and is never picked up by db push
CI check fails if any file in supabase/migrations/ lacks a valid ^[0-9]{14}_ timestamp prefix

userStories.title: Fix cross-tenant IDOR in execute-workflow / workflow-execution edge functions
userStories.description: As a tenant, I want workflow execution to verify the caller belongs to the workflow's company_id so an authenticated user of company A cannot trigger company B's automations (emails, task creation, webhooks) by guessing a workflowId. The function builds a SERVICE_ROLE_KEY client and reads workflow_definitions by caller-supplied id with zero identity/company check, so RLS gives no protection.
acceptanceCriteria: execute-workflow and workflow-execution resolve the caller's company_id from the JWT
Return 403 when target workflow_definitions.company_id != caller company_id
Replace wildcard CORS with the shared secure-cors helper
Regression test: a cross-company workflowId returns 403
userStories.notes: COMPLETED (2026-07-12). execute-workflow: added initializeAuthContext + authorizeWorkflowAccess ownership gate (service-role lookups of workflow/execution company_id -> verifyCompanyAccess -> 403) and secure-cors. workflow-execution: secure-cors + defense-in-depth verifyCompanyAccess assertion. New dependency-free _shared/workflow-auth.ts with vitest test (6 cases incl. cross-company 403) now run in CI via vitest include. CAVEAT: execute-workflow's execution BODY has pre-existing structural bugs (continueExecution undefined; startExecution reads undefined startIndex/execution) so it throws at runtime — flagged for a separate fix; the IDOR is closed at the boundary regardless.

userStories.title: Scope all FOR ALL USING(true) RLS policies to service_role (finish US-197 hardening)
userStories.description: As a Brikly customer, I want every system/service RLS policy scoped to service_role instead of public/authenticated so a logged-in user of one company cannot read another company's job-costing, document signatures, predictions, usage and behavioral rows. US-197 proved this class of bug is exploitable but patched only 3 of ~40+ tables; ~41 permissive policies remain.
acceptanceCriteria: Scripted audit enumerates all FOR ALL USING(true) policies lacking TO service_role
Each is scoped TO service_role or replaced with a company_id-scoped USING clause
Fix ships as append-only migrations following 20260613120000
CI check fails if a new policy uses USING(true) without TO service_role
userStories.notes: SUBSTANTIALLY COMPLETE (2026-07-12); 4 tables deferred. Shipped: (1) scripts/check-rls-policies.mjs audit+regression guard (baseline-grandfathered; fails on NEW permissive FOR ALL USING(true) without TO service_role), wired into CI + pre-commit; (2) migration 20260712120000 that dynamically (via live pg_policies, idempotent) scopes to service_role the permissive policies on 12 VERIFIED-SAFE tables: job_costing_summary, usage_metrics, document_signatures, project_predictions, prediction_performance, incident_metrics, affiliate_referrals, affiliate_rewards, workflow_step_executions, automated_workflow_executions, resource_availability_patterns, weather_forecasts (each either has a separate company-scoped SELECT the frontend reads through, or zero frontend access = edge-fn/service-role only). RESIDUAL LEAK — DEFERRED (need a company-scoped write policy added FIRST, then staging verification): workflow_executions, workflow_analytics, calendar_events, webhook_events (frontend writes directly). Intentionally-public/reference tables NOT touched: pseo_* , trades, seo_meta_tags, feature_announcements, ai_environment_config, oauth_pending_states, saml_pending_requests. Could not verify against live DB (no staging yet, US-247); migration is written to be safe on live state. || FOLLOW-UP (2026-08-27): the 'verified safe' analysis for the 12 scoped tables checked the FRONTEND but not edge functions that build their client from initializeAuthContext(). Three wrote scoped tables with a user-JWT client: track-usage and usage-billing (usage_metrics), workflow-execution (workflow_step_executions). Those tables are left with a company-scoped SELECT policy and nothing else once this migration lands, so a user-JWT write has no policy path - and every one of those call sites discarded the Supabase error, so it fails SILENTLY: usage stops being billed, workflow step history stops being written, handler still returns success. That means either 20260712120000 is not applied in production, or those three have been quietly failing since it was; there is no way to tell from the repo. All three now authorise the caller in the handler and write via createServiceClient() from _shared/service-client.ts, with the errors surfaced. scripts/check-rls-write-paths.mjs keeps the premise true (fails on a non-service-role write to any of the 12 tables); wired into pre-commit and CI. IF MORE TABLES ARE SCOPED LATER, add them to SERVICE_ROLE_ONLY in that script and re-run it before shipping the migration - that check is what the original 'verified safe' pass was missing. || DEFERRED FOUR ADDRESSED (2026-08-27) by migration 20260827023111, without scoping their permissive policies. Scoping would remove the only write path the frontend has, which CLAUDE.md rules out in a single release; instead each of workflow_executions, workflow_analytics and calendar_events gets a RESTRICTIVE company-scoped policy, and webhook_events (no company_id, platform-level) a RESTRICTIVE root_admin one. Restrictive policies AND rather than OR, so a same-company write still passes - no mixed-client window - while a cross-company write is denied whatever the permissive policy says. Granted TO authenticated, anon only, so service_role is unaffected regardless of BYPASSRLS. root_admin keeps cross-company access, matching each table's existing SELECT policy. THIS CLOSED A LIVE HOLE: src/services/WorkflowExecutionService.ts cancelExecution filters only by execution id, so with FOR ALL USING(true) OR'd in, any authenticated user could cancel any company's running workflow execution. The permissive policies on those four are still there and can be scoped later; if that happens, add the tables to SERVICE_ROLE_ONLY in scripts/check-rls-write-paths.mjs FIRST and run it - workflow-execution and sync-calendar write them with a user-JWT client today. That note is in the script. || SSO PENDING STATE (2026-08-27), the most serious find in this backlog: saml_pending_requests and oauth_pending_states were created with a policy NAMED 'Service role manages ...' that has no TO clause, so it is granted to PUBLIC - anon and authenticated, both reachable with the publishable key in the web bundle. oauth_pending_states stores the OAuth `state` and the PKCE `code_verifier`; sso-oauth-callback reads the verifier back and sends it with the token exchange (line ~266), so read access defeats PKCE for any code an attacker observes, and read/write access defeats the CSRF state check and allows seeding a chosen return_url. Scoped to service_role by 20260827030000 - safe with nothing on the other side, since no client code anywhere references either table and all three functions that do use a SERVICE_ROLE_KEY client. Both added to scripts/check-rls-write-paths.mjs. feature_announcements got a restrictive company scope (20260827031000); its publish path filtered only by id, so any authenticated user could publish another company's announcement. Remaining tables tracked in US-298 - each needs the live schema to settle, not more inference from migration source.

userStories.title: Gate cross-tenant analytics/cron edge functions to root_admin or cron secret
userStories.description: As the business owner, I want internal analytics/cron functions that aggregate across all tenants to reject non-admin callers so a client_portal or field_supervisor user cannot pull global MRR/ARR/churn or trigger expensive Stripe fan-out. calculate-revenue-metrics uses the service role, reads Stripe secret_key, returns company-wide financials, and performs no caller/role check while verify_jwt=true lets any authenticated user invoke it.
acceptanceCriteria: calculate-revenue-metrics, generate-churn-predictions, calculate-health-scores, auto-intervention-scheduler verify caller is root_admin OR present a CRON secret header
Return 403 for non-privileged callers
Intended invoker (cron vs admin) documented in config.toml
Audit all SERVICE_ROLE_KEY functions with no caller check for the same gap
userStories.notes: COMPLETED (2026-07-12) for the named cross-tenant analytics functions. Added requireSystemOrAdmin guard (admin JWT OR x-cron-secret) + secure-cors to calculate-revenue-metrics, generate-churn-predictions, auto-intervention-scheduler; calculate-health-scores was already guarded. config.toml annotated with intended invoker; kept verify_jwt=true deliberately (flipping to false would combine with requireSystemOrAdmin's staged-rollout 'allow when CRON_SECRET unset' to leave them fully open). OPS FOLLOW-UP: set CRON_SECRET in Supabase function env and have schedulers send x-cron-secret to fully enforce. AC4 (audit ALL service-role fns): heuristic flags 52 candidates but most are legitimately public or JWT-gated; a full sweep is deferred to a dedicated pass (overlaps US-241 Zod + US-244 CORS).

userStories.title: Roll out secure-cors helper across ~140 functions still using wildcard '*'
userStories.description: As a security owner, I want all edge functions to derive CORS from the shared getCorsHeaders(req) allowlist so only brikly.net/configured origins can invoke them from a browser. ~140 of ~191 functions hardcode Access-Control-Allow-Origin:'*' inline while only ~47 use the whitelist-based _shared/secure-cors.ts the team already built; even _shared/cors.ts still hardcodes '*'.
acceptanceCriteria: No function contains a literal 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin':'*' outside a documented public-webhook allowlist
All functions import getCorsHeaders/handleCorsPreflightRequest from secure-cors.ts
Deprecated wildcard _shared/cors.ts removed or repointed
CI grep guard rejects new wildcard-origin literals
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-08-27). Wildcard functions 137 -> 10, and all 10 remaining are intentionally cross-origin. AC1: no function ships a wildcard outside the documented public set (api-auth, capture-lead, handle-demo-request, handle-sales-contact, gsc-oauth-callback, google-calendar-callback, outlook-calendar-callback, webhook-verify, track-referral, process-referral-signup) - each authenticates its own caller and holds no cookie session. AC2: 127 functions converted to getCorsHeaders(req)/handleCorsPreflightRequest(req) from _shared/secure-cors.ts. AC3: _shared/cors.ts no longer defines a wildcard; it re-exports the pinned corsHeaders with a pointer to getCorsHeaders, and its one importer is on the per-request helper. AC4: scripts/check-cors-wildcards.mjs fails on any new wildcard, wired into .husky/pre-commit and the CI guard job, backlog now empty. THREE SHAPES were needed: (1) 94 with an inline serve() handler took a one-line edit; (2) 15 either had a named/default handler, or were false negatives from a hand-rolled tokenizer that mis-parsed regex literals - redone on the TypeScript compiler API; (3) 18 built responses in module-scope helpers, so corsHeaders is now a leading parameter threaded to every call site (leading, because a required parameter cannot follow the optional ones several helpers end with). VERIFICATION LIMIT: no Deno in the sandbox and deno.land is blocked by network policy, so edge functions cannot be typechecked. Verified instead with three AST passes (no wildcard + imports resolve; every corsHeaders use resolves to an enclosing parameter or local; every threaded-helper reference is a call passing corsHeaders first), esbuild parse on every changed file, and eslint at 0 errors. RUN deno check BEFORE DEPLOYING. SIDE EFFECT: functions that previously advertised a narrower Access-Control-Allow-Methods (oauth-proxy 'GET, POST, OPTIONS'; social-post-scheduler 'POST, OPTIONS') now advertise the shared 'GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS'. That widens the preflight answer only - each function still handles the methods it always did.

userStories.title: Enforce Zod input validation on mutating edge functions (currently 17 of ~193)
userStories.description: As a platform maintainer, I want every edge function that accepts a body to validate it with Zod so malformed/malicious payloads are rejected before hitting Postgres. Only 17 of ~193 functions validate; write-capable functions (change-orders, generate-invoice, projects, geofencing, change-subscription, execute-workflow) use req.json() fields raw, contradicting CLAUDE.md Security rule #2.
acceptanceCriteria: Shared validate(body, schema) helper in _shared returns the standard error envelope
Zod schemas added to the top ~30 mutating functions (financial, project, workflow, scheduling)
400 with { success:false, error } on validation failure
Lint/PR checklist requires a schema for any req.json() usage
userStories.notes: IN PROGRESS (2026-08-27). AC1 DONE: supabase/functions/_shared/validate-body.ts exports validateBody(req, schema, {name}) and returns the standard {success:false, error, timestamp} envelope via errorResponse(). AC3 DONE: the enforce path returns 400 with that envelope. AC4 DONE: scripts/check-edge-input-validation.mjs fails on a new function reading a body with no schema, or a converted one losing it; wired into .husky/pre-commit and the CI guard job. AC2 PARTIAL: 6 of the ~30 done - the ones the audit named (change-orders, geofencing, change-subscription, generate-invoice, execute-workflow, projects). Backlog 133 of 156. STAGED ROLLOUT, READ THIS BEFORE ADDING MORE: validation defaults to report mode, not enforce. CLAUDE.md's Backward Compatibility section rules out tightening an input schema in a single release - an iOS client at MIN_SUPPORTED_IOS_VERSION sending an unexpected shape would start getting 400s with no way to update, and there is no staging project to discover that on (US-247 still open). In report mode a failing parse logs '[input-validation] <fn> would reject: <field paths>' and the handler receives the raw body unchanged. Set INPUT_VALIDATION_MODE=enforce on the Supabase project to flip every function at once, with no code change. Do that only after watching those log lines for a full release cycle. A body that is not JSON at all is rejected in both modes. SECURITY FINDING fixed along the way: projects spread the raw body into insert() and update(), so any writable column was settable, including id, created_by and created_at. RLS blocks the cross-tenant move (projects_update declares no WITH CHECK, so Postgres applies its USING clause to the new row too, and initializeAuthContext uses the anon key with the caller's JWT so RLS does apply) - but nothing stopped a caller rewriting provenance columns inside their own company. Both paths now go through a column allowlist, applied unconditionally rather than staged. MASS-ASSIGNMENT SWEEP DONE (2026-08-27): AST sweep over all edge functions for writes that spread a request body into insert/update/upsert, following variable aliases. Three sites, all fixed behind _shared/writable-columns.ts. See US-297 for the two real findings. Backlog now 132 of 156; 8 of the ~30 target functions have schemas (change-orders, change-subscription, execute-workflow, generate-invoice, geofencing, projects, time-tracking x2). PROGRESS 2026-08-27: took the money functions first - process-refund, store-stripe-keys, remove-payment-method, set-default-payment-method. Backlog 132 -> 128, schemas 24 -> 28, all in report mode via validateBody so nothing 400s until INPUT_VALIDATION_MODE flips. THE FIND WAS NOT A SCHEMA GAP. remove-payment-method authenticated the caller and then called stripe.paymentMethods.detach(payment_method_id) on whatever id the body carried, with no check that the method belonged to them - and the Stripe key there is the platform own, so every customer is in scope. Any signed-in user who learned another customer pm_ id could detach it and break their next renewal. detach() offers no protection of its own; set-default-payment-method happens to be safe only because customers.update rejects a method that is not attached to that customer. Now resolves the caller company stripe_customer_id, retrieves the payment method, and compares - returning the same 404 as a genuine miss, because a distinct 403 would confirm the id exists. Worth stating plainly: adding Zod would NOT have caught this. A well-formed pm_ id belonging to someone else passes every schema. Validation and authorisation are different problems and this story only covers one of them. Second real gap, this one a schema issue: process-refund took amount as an unbounded number while the approval gate is amount > 100 - so a NEGATIVE amount is false for that test, skips approval, and lands in the refunds ledger as a negative row. Now positive, two decimal places, ceiling 1,000,000. store-stripe-keys is well authorised already (checks the caller own profile company matches company_id and requires admin) - its gap was shape only: secret_key was unvalidated and would have been encrypted and stored as whatever it was, surfacing only when a charge failed. Now pattern-matched to sk_/rk_ test|live, and webhook_secret to whsec_. PROGRESS 2026-08-27 (2): applied the authorisation lens rather than the schema lens, since that is what paid off in the first batch. Wrote an AST scan for the shape that matters - a value destructured from req.json() reaching .eq(company_id|user_id|tenant_id|subscriber_id|account_id, X) - and found 44 sites across about 20 functions. Most are harmless: they use a user-JWT client, so RLS enforces the tenancy regardless of what the body claims. Exactly two used a SERVICE-ROLE client with a body-supplied id and no caller check. (1) send-push-notification authenticated the caller and then looked up push_subscriptions for a body user_id with the service role. Any signed-in user could push an arbitrary title, body, icon and data payload to ANY other user - a phishing message delivered through Brikly own notification channel, on the lock screen, with Brikly icon. Now resolves both profiles in one query and requires the same company_id, returning the existing no-subscriptions response rather than a distinct error so it cannot be used to probe which user ids exist. (2) social-post-redeploy had NO AUTHENTICATION AT ALL - straight from req.json() to a service-role client filtered on the body company_id. It is not in supabase/config.toml so verify_jwt defaults to true, but that only means presents a valid project JWT, and THE PUBLISHABLE ANON KEY IS ONE and ships in the client bundle. So anyone holding the anon key could name any company_id, read that company automated_social_posts_config including its webhook_url plus their last twelve social posts, and fire their webhook. Now requires initializeAuthContext and checks the caller profile company against the body, returning 404. That verify_jwt distinction is worth carrying: it is a gateway signature check, not authentication, and treating it as the latter is how this one looked covered. Backlog 128 -> 126, schemas 28 -> 30. PROGRESS 2026-08-27 (3): generalised the verify_jwt finding instead of fixing one more function by hand. Swept every edge function for handler-level caller verification and found 46 with none. Most are anonymous by design (signup/OTP, OAuth and SAML callbacks, lead capture, health-check). Two were not, and both were reachable on the anon key alone: webhook-trigger took tenant_id from the body with a service-role client and read plus FIRED every webhook_endpoint for that tenant - enumerate any customer webhook URLs, then post arbitrary data into their downstream systems; send-usage-alert took companyId the same way and read every admin email address for that company before emailing them - harvest admin addresses per company and send them Brikly-branded mail. Neither had a live caller: nothing invokes webhook-trigger at all, and send-usage-alert only invocation is COMMENTED OUT in track-usage. Both now require _shared/internal-only.ts requireInternalCaller, which accepts the service-role bearer or the CRON_SECRET header, NEVER fails open when neither is configured (a misconfigured internal endpoint should be unreachable, not public), and answers 404 rather than 403 so the endpoint is not confirmed to exist. 7 unit tests including the anon-key case that verify_jwt would have accepted. NEW GUARD check-unauthenticated-edge-functions.mjs, in pre-commit and CI, with 27 public-by-design entries and 16 grandfathered ones still needing the public/internal/user-auth decision. Also CORRECTED THE DOCSTRING of check-edge-function-auth.mjs, which asserted that Supabase enforces a valid JWT for verify_jwt = true functions as though that were sufficient - that sentence is why this whole class went unexamined. It now says plainly that verify_jwt is a signature check, that the anon key satisfies it, and which guard covers the gap. Backlog unchanged at 126 (these two already had no Zod either, but the authorisation was the point). PROGRESS 2026-08-27 (4): triaged four of the sixteen grandfathered functions, chosen because they are invoked from the BROWSER by a signed-in user, so the right answer is user auth rather than internal-only. send-notification is the worst of them: it takes to as a body-supplied email address and sends through Resend as Brikly <notifications@resend.dev>, with no auth. Anyone holding the anon key had an OPEN MAIL RELAY on Brikly Resend account and sending reputation - arbitrary recipient, arbitrary subject and body, Brikly name on it. Beyond the phishing use, that is how a sending domain gets blacklisted. Note it already had a careful Zod schema (to: z.string().email(), etc.) and that helped not at all: every field was well-formed, and the missing check was WHO not WHAT. Third time today that distinction has decided a finding. send-support-notification is the same shape twice over - it mails support@brikly.net and a body-supplied customerEmail. send-safety-notification sends incident mail under Brikly name to body-named addresses. document-classifier spends money per call on a model provider. All four now call initializeAuthContext. Baseline 16 -> 12. REMAINING 12, each still needing the public/internal/user-auth decision: analyze-support-ticket, blog-ai-automation, blog_social_webhook, create-missing-content, enhanced-blog-ai-simple, send-seo-notification, seo-backend-integration, seo-file-generator, social-content-generator, social-post-scheduler, social-webhook-deployer, trigger-expo-build. Of those, blog-ai-automation, seo-backend-integration and trigger-expo-build have NO caller anywhere in the repo, so internal-only is likely right for them. PROGRESS 2026-08-27 (5): finished the caller-verification triage - the guard baseline is now EMPTY. Every edge function verifies its caller, inside its handler. Split by what actually invokes each: five browser-invoked ones got initializeAuthContext (create-missing-content, enhanced-blog-ai-simple, seo-file-generator, social-content-generator, social-webhook-deployer); two invoked by another edge function with a service-role client got requireInternalCaller (blog_social_webhook from enhanced-blog-ai-fixed, send-seo-notification from run-scheduled-audit - both verified to pass the service-role bearer before requiring it); five with NO caller anywhere in the repo got requireInternalCaller (analyze-support-ticket, blog-ai-automation, seo-backend-integration, social-post-scheduler, trigger-expo-build). I ADDED TWO OF THESE IN THE WRONG PLACE. Applying them by script, the checks for social-content-generator and blog_social_webhook landed inside helper functions (getRecentFormats, getInstagramMediaFromStorage) rather than the handler. They compiled, because req was in scope through the closure, and the guard - which matched on name only - reported both as covered. A check that runs in the wrong function is worse than none, because it reads as done. Caught by verifying separately that each guard call sits after the handler declaration. The guard now enforces that itself, on the AST: it locates the handler passed to serve() or Deno.serve() or assigned to a handler variable, and requires the guard call to be lexically inside it. That immediately flagged five more - four were my own detector missing Deno.serve (a PropertyAccessExpression, not a bare identifier), and api-management was a genuine delegation, where every route function validates a hashed API key through validateApiRequest and only createApiKey uses auth.getUser. Added validateApiRequest/validateApiKey to the recognised set and a DELEGATES map that names the delegate explicitly and requires it to contain the check - deliberately NOT a blanket one-level-of-delegation rule, because that would have accepted the two real misplacements this check exists for. Mutation-tested with a function whose guard sits in a helper.

userStories.title: Add per-user rate limiting to expensive AI, email, and report edge functions
userStories.description: As an operator, I want expensive AI-generation, email, and report functions to enforce per-user/company rate limits via the existing _shared/rate-limiter.ts so a compromised token cannot run up LLM/SES bills or spam customers. The limiter exists but only ~18 functions use it; generate-blog-content, enhanced-blog-ai, generate-*-forecast, process-voice-command, voice-to-text, send-email, generate-custom-report, smart-data-analyzer are unprotected. Distinct from US-205 (DoS wiring).
acceptanceCriteria: All AI-generation functions enforce rate limits keyed by user+company
send-email and other SES-backed senders enforce send limits
Report generators rate-limited
429 responses use the standard envelope and are documented for iOS
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-08-27). 14 functions that cost money per call now enforce a per-caller ceiling, up from the handful that did. AC1 (AI): generate-blog-content, enhanced-blog-ai, smart-data-analyzer, generate-cash-flow-forecast, voice-to-text, process-voice-command, generate-custom-report added; ai-estimating, ai-content-generator, analyze-support-ticket already had one. Keyed on user id, not IP - an IP ceiling is shared by everyone behind one customer's NAT and a stolen token walks around it by changing address. AC2 (email): signup-with-otp had NO throttle at all - unauthenticated, sends mail, no ceiling, so an open relay for bombing an address or burning SES quota. reset-password-otp had a per-email throttle but no per-IP one, so one source could spray across many addresses without tripping it. send-email is the generic sender. All three now use the AUTH preset. THE TWO CONTROLS ARE DIFFERENT AND BOTH ARE WANTED: per-email stops one address being targeted, per-IP stops one source spraying. send-auth-otp already had both and is the model. AC3 (reports): generate-custom-report. AC4 (envelope): rateLimitResponse now emits success:false and timestamp alongside the existing error/retryAfter/limit/requestCount, so it matches CLAUDE.md's shape without breaking a client reading the old fields - additive, per the backward-compat rules. Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* headers unchanged, which is what iOS should actually key on. NEW: _shared/rate-limiter.ts exports enforceRateLimit(client, identifier, endpoint, preset, cors) which collapses check-and-429 into one call. Pass a SERVICE-ROLE client - rate_limit_violations is not the caller's to read or write, and using their JWT would make the limit depend on RLS. process-voice-command is the cautionary case: it takes user_id in its BODY, which is exactly what must not be the key, since a caller can rotate a body field and never hit a limit. It and voice-to-text resolve the user from the token instead and fall back to IP only where there is none, so a service-key path still works. KNOWN TRADE, documented on the helper: checkRateLimit returns allowed when it cannot reach the database, so a limiter outage never blocks legitimate traffic - but it also removes the ceiling. These calls want provider-side spend caps (OpenAI, SES) as the backstop; that is not something the repo can enforce. GUARD: scripts/check-rate-limit-coverage.mjs tracks all 14 and fails if one loses its limit. Mutation-checked. In pre-commit and CI. NOT LIMITED, deliberately: send-payment-reminder, send-scheduled-emails, send-usage-alert and the other cron-driven senders. A ceiling there would throttle scheduled work rather than an abuser.

userStories.title: Add error tracking to Supabase edge functions (currently console.log only)

Sentry is wired only in the web frontend; 193 functions report errors via console.log/console.error with no aggregation or alerting. US-172 covers iOS Sentry only.
acceptanceCriteria: Shared _shared/observability.ts initializes a Deno-compatible Sentry client gated on EDGE_SENTRY_DSN
Top-level catches wrapped in stripe-webhook, quickbooks-sync, process-funnel-queue, process-dunning, send-* first
Events tagged with function name, company_id, request id; tokens/PII scrubbed
EDGE_SENTRY_DSN documented and set; a crash smoke test asserts events reach Sentry
userStories.notes: AC1/AC2/AC3 DONE (2026-08-27); AC4 partially - the DSN is documented but the smoke test needs a real Sentry project. AC1: _shared/observability.ts, gated on EDGE_SENTRY_DSN. It posts to Sentry's HTTP ENVELOPE endpoint with plain fetch rather than importing a Deno SDK. That was a deliberate choice, not a workaround: a URL import costs cold-start time on every invocation of every function, the envelope format is a documented stable API, and having zero dependencies is what makes the module testable under vitest - edge-function entry points import Deno URL modules vitest cannot load, so anything worth testing has to live in _shared. AC2: wired into the top-level catches of stripe-webhook, quickbooks-sync, process-dunning and process-funnel-queue. The last two are cron-driven, where nobody reads the response and self-reporting is the only way a failure surfaces at all. AC3: events tagged with function name, company_id, user id and request id. Scrubbing runs over the WHOLE event rather than a list of known fields - sensitive keys by name at any depth, plus secret-shaped values wherever they appear including inside a message string (JWTs, sk_live/sk_test, whsec_, bearer tokens, email addresses). An error message is exactly where a key leaks, so matching on shape matters as much as on key name. NEVER THROWS, NEVER REJECTS - on a bad DSN, a dead network, or a 429 from Sentry. Reporting an error must not be able to cause one; same rule as the audit writer in US-244. 16 tests, mutation-checked on the two properties that matter: dropping key redaction fails, letting a transport failure escape fails. AC4 REMAINING: EDGE_SENTRY_DSN is documented in env.example as a SUPABASE SECRET, not a build variable - it is read at runtime via Deno.env and must not reach the web bundle. Set it with `supabase secrets set EDGE_SENTRY_DSN=...`, then throw deliberately in one function and confirm the event lands. Until it is set, captureException is a no-op and handlers still log to the platform's own logs - they just do not aggregate or alert. REMAINING SCOPE: the story lists send-* as well. Those were left for a follow-up pass; the four wired here are the ones where a silent failure costs money or data.

userStories.title: Paginate QuickBooks sync and add 429 retry to prevent silent data loss
userStories.description: As an accounting user at a larger company, I want the QuickBooks import to page through all customers/items/expenses/payments and retry on throttling so my sync isn't silently truncated at the first 100-1000 records or aborted by a 429. quickbooks-sync issues 'SELECT * FROM {entity}' with no STARTPOSITION/MAXRESULTS and no 429 handling.
acceptanceCriteria: fetchQuickBooksData loops STARTPOSITION/MAXRESULTS until a short page returns
HTTP 429 / QB throttle detected and retried with backoff honoring Retry-After
quickbooks_sync_logs records total-available vs processed so truncation is visible
Test with a mocked >1000-record response asserts all pages are fetched
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-08-27). AC1: fetchQuickBooksData pages STARTPOSITION/MAXRESULTS in windows of 500 until a page comes back shorter than the window. QuickBooks has no next-page cursor, so a short page is the only end signal available. A 200-page ceiling guards against an endless loop if the API ever stops advancing, and hitting it sets truncated:true rather than pretending the import was complete. AC2: 429, 503 and 500 retried up to 4 times, honouring Retry-After when Intuit sends it and backing off exponentially (capped at 30s) when it does not. 401 is deliberately NOT retried - a bad token does not fix itself and retrying only delays the reconnect prompt the user needs to see. AC3: quickbooks_sync_logs now carries records_fetched alongside records_processed, plus truncated_entities and throttle_retries. Equal fetched/processed means everything QuickBooks returned was written; a gap means rows were dropped on our side. That is the distinction that makes a truncated import visible rather than just looking like a small account. AC4: 9 tests in supabase/functions/_shared/quickbooks-paging.test.ts, including a >2000-row mocked response asserting every page is fetched and every row distinct. Mutation-checked: reverting to a single unpaged request fails 2, dropping the throttle retry fails 4, ignoring Retry-After fails 1. STRUCTURAL NOTE: the paging logic moved to _shared/quickbooks-paging.ts with an injectable fetchImpl and sleep. quickbooks-sync/index.ts imports Deno URL modules which vitest cannot load, so logic that needs testing has to live in _shared - that is the general rule for edge functions in this repo until Deno is available in CI. SCHEMA: records_fetched, truncated_entities and throttle_retries did not exist on quickbooks_sync_logs, so the log update would have named columns PostgREST rejects - and that update discards its error (US-300), so the whole log write would have failed silently while the sync reported success. Migration 20260827050000 adds all three as nullable JSONB/INTEGER with no backfill: additive per CLAUDE.md, and historical rows genuinely have no answer for these rather than a zero. Caught by checking the generated types before shipping - worth doing for any write naming a new column, because the failure is silent wherever the error is unread.

userStories.notes: PROPOSED (deep-dive audit 2026-07-12). Theme: Code Health. SEV: MEDIUM. Source: Architecture audit. Feeds US-212. PARTIAL (2026-07-12): deleted the stray dead src/integrations/supabase/types-N-DPEARSON.ts (3181 lines, referenced nowhere in code). Regenerating types.ts is BLOCKED here — needs SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN + the supabase CLI (neither available in this environment); run `supabase gen types typescript --project-id brikly > src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` locally to finish. PROGRESS 2026-08-27: AC1 already satisfied - types-N-DPEARSON.ts is gone from the tree and from git ls-files (removed during the US-261 cruft sweep). AC3 done, and it turned up a real footgun in the process. The db:types script was . Shell redirection TRUNCATES THE TARGET BEFORE THE COMMAND RUNS, so any failure - no network, expired access token, wrong project id, CLI not installed - left a 41,282-line types file at zero bytes and the whole app uncompilable. The failure mode was strictly worse than not running it at all. Replaced with scripts/gen-supabase-types.mjs, which generates to a temp file, sanity-checks it (non-empty, has export type Json, has export type Database, has a Tables block, and is not less than half the size of what it would replace), and only then moves it into place. Verified three failure paths leave types.ts byte-identical: CLI absent (ENOENT), a CLI that exits 0 printing an auth error, and a CLI that exits 0 with a two-table schema. types.ts now carries a DO NOT EDIT BY HAND banner naming the regeneration command, and the script strips and re-adds that banner so it survives regeneration rather than being lost on the first run. AC2 still needs live DB access - supabase gen types reaches the running project, which I cannot. AC4 measurement is running. AC4 MEASURED 2026-08-27 (npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json, 1842 errors total against the 1860 baseline): TS2339 is 341, not the 396 this story recorded - the gap is US-212 work already landed, not schema drift resolving itself. Distribution: 133 in src/components, 84 in src/hooks, 64 in src/services, 55 in src/pages, 5 in src/lib. Across 57 files, of which 42 contain a supabase query (from(...) or .rpc(...)) and 15 do not. Those 42 files hold 250 of the 341; the other 91 are in files that never touch Supabase and so cannot be schema drift. 90 of the 341 name never, SelectQueryError, GenericStringError or ParserError as the type the property is missing from - that specific set is the signature of a query whose generated row type resolved to never, which is what stale types produce, so it is the highest-confidence subset. Reading: roughly 250 are plausibly schema-drift-driven and about 90 of those are near-certain, while at least 91 will survive regenerating types.ts and belong to US-212 rather than here. Worth re-running this exact breakdown after AC2 lands to see how many actually clear - the difference between 250 and 90 is the honest uncertainty in the estimate.

userStories.title: INCIDENT: purge committed production DB dump from git history and rotate exposed secrets
userStories.description: A real 20.6MB PostgreSQL cluster dump (backups/db_cluster-17-12-2025.backup + two .gz copies) was committed to the repo. It contains auth.users, auth.refresh_tokens, auth.sessions, auth.mfa_factors, pgsodium.key (encryption keys), ~24,000 JWTs, and service_role/stripe/secret_key values across 538 tables — i.e. full production data and live credentials. US-261 removed it from the working tree, but it remains in git history and must be purged and all exposed secrets rotated. As a security owner, I want the dump purged from history and every credential it exposed rotated so a repo-access holder cannot extract customer data or live tokens.
acceptanceCriteria: Purge backups/*.backup* from all git history (git filter-repo or BFG) on main, develop, and this branch; coordinate the force-push and notify collaborators to re-clone
Rotate the Supabase service_role key and JWT secret; invalidate all existing auth sessions/refresh tokens (forces re-login)
Rotate any Stripe keys and other API keys/secrets stored in dumped tables (stripe_keys, ai_model_configurations, etc.) and re-key pgsodium
Review who had repo access while the dump was present; assess breach-notification obligations for the exposed PII
Confirm no other DB dump or secret-bearing artifact remains in history (gitleaks --full history scan)
userStories.notes: CRITICAL — discovered 2026-07-12 during US-261 cruft cleanup. Requires history rewrite (force-push, coordinated) + credential rotation; NOT auto-remediable in this loop. Escalated to the user for immediate action. Remediation runbook drafted at docs/RUNBOOK_DB_DUMP_INCIDENT.md (containment + rotation + git filter-repo purge commands for the 3 blob paths + access-review/breach checklist). Ready for the user to execute — still requires their Supabase/Stripe/GitHub-admin access; not auto-remediable. || UPDATE 2026-08-27, three findings, all of which change what the remediation has to do. (1) A FOURTH DUMP, and it was NOT only in history - backup/db_cluster-11-12-2025@04-13-16.backup.gz was still present in HEAD on this branch. US-261 removed backups/ and missed backup/, singular. Anyone cloning the repo today got a 1.4MB PostgreSQL database cluster dump carrying the same pgsodium_* roles and 973 matches for service_role/sk_live/sk_test/refresh_token/pgsodium. It has now been removed from tracking - that is containment only; the blob is still in history and the purge and rotation are unchanged and still need the user. Introduced in commit e26c295, whose subject is about a logo component. (2) THE RUNBOOK WOULD HAVE LEFT IT BEHIND. It listed three paths under backups/, its shortcut was --path backups/ --invert-paths, and its verification was git rev-list --all --objects | grep -i backups - so the fourth would have survived the purge AND the check would have returned nothing and read as clean. Runbook corrected: four paths, both directories in the shortcut, and verification now greps a pattern (.backup|.dump|.sql.gz|db_cluster) plus a size sweep, because the next one may not be named like a backup at all. (3) THE PREVENTION GUARD DID NOT WORK. check-no-tracked-cruft.sh matched .backup$, which does not match .backup.gz - three of the four dumps are .backup.gz, so it would have stopped exactly one of them, while this runbook described it as already blocking re-commits. It also anchored ^backup_.*.sql$ to the start of the path and had no pattern for a backup directory at all. Rewritten to cover both directory names, every compression suffix, .dump/.pgdump/.sql.gz, backup_*.sql at any depth, and db_cluster anywhere; mutation-tested against seven shapes, five of which the old pattern missed. .gitignore extended to match. AC5 IS DONE: enumerated every path in git rev-list --objects --all against secret-bearing patterns and separately by blob size. Those four dumps are the only such artifacts - package.json.backup and tests/fullGithuboutput.txt both scan clean for JWTs, sk_live/sk_test, service_role, GitHub tokens and PEM blocks, and every other blob over 2MB is marketing video under media/assets/. AC1-AC4 still need the user: force-push on protected branches and credential rotation are not mine to do.
