Baseline 20 -> 17, with a verdict recorded against each in the guard header. THREE DELETED. (1) src/services/SecurityService.ts was entirely mock: updateSecuritySettings and resolveSecurityAlert each showed a success toast and returned true with an EMPTY try body, writing nothing, so an admin toggling MFA-required would see Security settings updated successfully and change nothing; performSecurityScan returned a hardcoded score of 85 and two invented issues; getSecuritySettings returned Mock security settings. Its checkRateLimit had already been converted to throw earlier in this session. The decisive detail: it NAME-COLLIDES with the live src/lib/security/securityService.ts, which SecureRoute.tsx and useAuthorization.ts genuinely use - so importing SecurityService could plausibly get the mock. That is the adoption hazard this AC is about, in its clearest form. (2) src/hooks/useAuth.ts was a second useAuth resolving the role through the get_user_primary_role RPC while the app own comes from AuthContext. I checked whether the unreferenced one was the MORE secure of the two before deleting - it is not; both read server-side, and AuthContext calls that same RPC at line 439. A duplicate, not a fix. (3) src/contexts/MockAuthContext.tsx was a test double sitting in production source next to the real AuthContext, hardcoding role: admin and a real production company UUID with the comment Real company ID from database. KEPT as real-but-unreferenced: secureLogger, sessionFingerprint, dosProtection, mobile/utils/permissions, useActiveSessions, useMFASetup, components/mfa/index. Checked dosProtection specifically because it showed four permissive returns - they are branches of a real analysis (config disabled, IP whitelisted, low risk score), not blanket permissiveness. The rest of the list is unrouted UI, not logic.

userStories.title: increment_session_calculations and increment_lead_score are called but do not exist
userStories.description: As a sales lead, I want lead scoring to actually score leads. src/lib/calculatorAnalytics.ts calls supabase.rpc('increment_lead_score', ...) in three places and supabase.rpc('increment_session_calculations', ...) in one, but neither function is defined in any migration under supabase/migrations. Until US-212's TS2551 fix those calls were dead anyway - they used .catch() on a PostgrestBuilder, which has no catch(), so a TypeError was thrown before the request was ever sent. Now the calls are genuinely attempted and log when the RPC is missing, which is how this became visible. So: decide whether lead scoring is a feature. If it is, add the two functions as migrations (increment_lead_score(p_lead_id uuid, p_points int) and increment_session_calculations(p_session_id text)) and confirm the columns they increment exist. If it is not, delete the call sites rather than leaving code that logs a missing-function error on every calculator interaction.
acceptanceCriteria: increment_lead_score and increment_session_calculations either exist as migrations or their call sites are removed
If added, each is SECURITY DEFINER with an explicit search_path and scoped so a caller cannot score another company's leads
Lead score changes are observable — a calculator interaction moves the score
No console error is logged on the normal path
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-08-27 while mining TS2551 for US-212. The generated types are stale (US-263), so 'not in types.ts' would not have been evidence on its own - the check was against the migration SQL, which is the source of truth for what has been created. Note the RPCs may still exist in the live database if they were created by hand outside a migration, which is its own problem and exactly what US-248 (an auditable migration-to-prod pipeline) is meant to prevent. Confirm against the live schema before adding a migration that might collide.

userStories.title: Sanitization tests ran under a DOM that breaks DOMPurify
userStories.description: As a security reviewer, I want the XSS test suite to actually prove the sanitizer works. vitest.config.ts sets environment: happy-dom for the whole suite. happy-dom 20.11.1 does not implement the DOM spec's NodeIterator pre-removing steps: when the node the iterator is positioned on is removed, iteration ends instead of the reference moving to the next node. DOMPurify sanitizes by walking the parsed tree with createNodeIterator and removing disallowed nodes as it goes, so under happy-dom it stops at the first node it strips and returns the remainder of the document untouched. Minimal reproduction: iterate four elements with createNodeIterator and remove the second. jsdom visits all four; happy-dom visits two and stops. Consequence: DOMPurify.sanitize('HelloW') returns 'W' under happy-dom and 'HelloW' under jsdom. This is a test-environment defect, not a sanitizer defect - the same DOMPurify 3.4.12 and the same sanitize.ts are correct under jsdom and in a browser. But it means six test files, 616 assertions, were giving no assurance at all, and one of them (useSanitizedForm 'prevents script injection in HTML fields') was failing outright. US-213 makes Unit Tests a required merge check, so that red test would block every merge once the rulesets are applied. Fix: declare @vitest-environment jsdom on the test files that reach DOMPurify, and add a guard that computes the DOMPurify taint set as a fixpoint over the src/ import graph so a new sanitizer wrapper or a new test for one cannot be added without the docblock.
acceptanceCriteria: Every test file whose assertions depend on DOMPurify declares @vitest-environment jsdom
scripts/check-sanitizer-test-env.mjs fails when such a file lacks the docblock, and runs in both .husky/pre-commit and the CI Security Smoke Tests job
The guard derives its taint set from the import graph rather than a hardcoded file list, and exempts only files with a written reason
npm run test:run is green, including useSanitizedForm > XSS Prevention > prevents script injection in HTML fields
The guard no-ops with an explanatory message if the suite default is ever switched to jsdom, so it cannot outlive its reason
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-08-27 chasing a single failing test after commit d8fae33. The lead was a comment already in src/lib/security/sanitize.ts on stripHtml - "in some environments DOMPurify with an empty allowlist still leaves inline tags in the output" - so someone hit this before and worked around it with a regex post-pass for stripHtml only, never diagnosing the cause or covering sanitizeHtml. Verified by minimal reproduction (NodeIterator + removal, happy-dom vs jsdom side by side) rather than by assuming "it works in a real browser". Deliberately did NOT switch the suite default to jsdom: a full-suite jsdom run was still going after 30 minutes against roughly 4 minutes under happy-dom, and the six files that need it finish in 4.3s. Deliberately did NOT add a regex element-allowlist post-pass to sanitizeHtml either - regex post-passes are what produced the original misdiagnosis. Open question worth its own story: src/lib/validations exports a SECOND function also named sanitizeHtml that is regex-based and strips everything between < and >, unrelated to the DOMPurify one.

userStories.title: create_document_version let any caller rewrite another company's document
userStories.description: As any authenticated user of any company, I could replace the file behind another company's document. public.create_document_version(p_document_id, p_file_path, p_file_size, p_checksum, p_version_notes) is SECURITY DEFINER with search_path = '', so it runs past RLS on both public.documents and public.document_versions, and it carried no authorisation check of its own. Passing an arbitrary p_document_id inserted a version row against that document, bumped its version number, and - the damaging part - ran UPDATE public.documents SET file_path = p_file_path WHERE id = p_document_id. file_path is what every reader downloads, so this silently repoints another company's document at a file the caller controls, leaving nothing behind but an updated_at bump. Found 2026-08-27 while verifying that document_versions.file_path stores a raw storage path, for the US-289 company-documents read policy.
acceptanceCriteria: create_document_version refuses a p_document_id whose document belongs to another company
The refusal raises insufficient_privilege rather than silently no-oping, so the client sees a failure
A NULL company_id is not denied - historical rows written before company_id was reliably set must stay versionable
The signature, parameter names, defaults and return type are unchanged, so PostgREST still resolves calls from clients at MIN_SUPPORTED_IOS_VERSION
A test pins the guard against the latest definition of the function, not a hardcoded migration filename
userStories.notes: FIXED 2026-08-27 in migration 20260827070000_scope_create_document_version.sql, which CREATE OR REPLACEs the function rather than editing the merged 20250801021602 that introduced it. The guard denies only the genuine cross-tenant case: a document that exists, carries a non-NULL company_id, and whose company is not the caller's, with root_admin exempted. It deliberately does not deny NULL company_id - DocumentManagement writes company_id from userProfile?.company_id and can persist NULL, and denying those would strand versioning on historical rows with no user-facing recovery. That is the same NULL-tenancy trap that made me drop seo_meta_tags from the restrictive-RLS work earlier in this session. A non-existent document id still fails on the document_versions FK, unchanged. Per CLAUDE.md this is a tightening, which is normally a multi-release change; it ships in one because the only calls whose behaviour changes are cross-tenant writes no legitimate client makes - the same reasoning as the RESTRICTIVE policy work in US-298. Note there are two overloads of this name: the 2-arg (p_document_id, p_version_data jsonb) from 20250126230001 and this 5-arg one. PostgREST resolves by named arguments, so the app's 5-key call reaches this one. The 2-arg overload is unreferenced by the app and unscoped; worth retiring, but dropping a function is destructive and needs its own release.

userStories.title: The audit trail was writable by anyone, including anon
userStories.description: As a security owner, I want the audit trail to be evidence rather than a guestbook. public.audit_logs carries two permissive INSERT policies, neither with a TO clause, so both grant PUBLIC: 'System can insert audit logs' (20250703164308, FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (true)) and 'site_audit_logs_insert' (20251203000002, same body - it dropped the SELECT policies it replaced but not this INSERT one). Permissive policies OR together, so authenticated and anon could both insert arbitrary rows. Every column an investigator would trust is caller-supplied: user_id, company_id, action_type, risk_level, description, created_at. That allows fabricating entries against another user, planting them in another company's trail, and burying a real event under noise. CLAUDE.md makes logging critical actions to the audit trail non-negotiable, which is exactly what makes a forgeable trail load-bearing.
acceptanceCriteria: authenticated and anon cannot INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE rows in audit_logs
Service-role and in-database (SECURITY DEFINER / trigger) writers are unaffected
The existing SELECT policies still govern reads - the fix does not widen or narrow who can read the trail
The merged permissive policies are not edited, per the append-only migration rule
A test pins the policy as RESTRICTIVE - the same body as PERMISSIVE would grant rather than deny
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-08-27 while working US-299, whose premise was the opposite: it recorded that audit_logs 'has only SELECT policies - there is no INSERT policy for authenticated or anon - so every one of those inserts is rejected by RLS'. That was wrong, and the correction is worse than the original story. FIXED in 20260827080000_restrict_audit_log_client_writes.sql with a RESTRICTIVE FOR ALL policy TO authenticated, anon: USING (true) so reads stay with the existing SELECT policies, WITH CHECK (false) so no client write passes. Restrictive rather than scoping the permissive policies because those are merged and cannot be edited, and because restrictive policies are AND'd - there is no window where a legitimate writer loses its path. FOR ALL rather than FOR INSERT so a later UPDATE or DELETE policy without a TO clause cannot reopen the hole from the other direction. Nothing legitimate loses a write: edge writers (_shared/audit-log.ts, verify-domain) construct SERVICE_ROLE_KEY clients, the in-database writers are SECURITY DEFINER functions and the BEFORE INSERT trigger from 20250202000012 which run as the table owner, and the only browser-side writer is useSecurityMonitor, which is mounted nowhere. Same shape as the oauth_pending_states find earlier in this session: a policy NAMED 'System can ...' with no TO clause, which reads as service-only and grants PUBLIC. Worth a sweep for the rest of that naming pattern. Also fixed scripts/check-rls-policies.mjs, which flagged this migration - it treated AS RESTRICTIVE ... USING (true) as a permissive grant. A restrictive USING (true) is a no-op for reads; the deny is in its WITH CHECK. Left unfixed, the guard would have pushed authors towards deleting the policies that close these holes. Mutation-tested both directions. FOLLOW-UP 2026-08-27 (same day): swept the whole class. A scan of the migration history for permissive policies with WITH CHECK (true) or a non-FOR-ALL USING (true), no TO clause, and not AS RESTRICTIVE, found 68. Of those, 10 are written by nothing in src/ (verified by matching insert/upsert/update/delete against every from(<table>) call across the repo) and carry real weight: data_access_logs, document_access_logs, sensitive_data_access_log, security_logs, security_metrics, api_request_logs, ddos_detection_logs, rate_limit_state, affiliate_codes. Two of those are not record-keeping at all - rate_limit_state had an open INSERT and an open UPDATE, so a client could reset the counter throttling it, defeating US-243 entirely; affiliate_codes had the same pair, so a caller could mint a referral code or change its commission. 20260827090000 denies client writes on all ten with the same RESTRICTIVE technique. Converting them surfaced four edge-function writes to security_logs still using a user-JWT client (setup-mfa once, sso-manage three times); those are now createServiceClient(), and all ten tables were added to check-rls-write-paths.mjs so a user-JWT write cannot come back. That guard also had a blind spot: it only recognised a service client held in a variable, so the inline createServiceClient().from(...) form the repo uses everywhere read as unrecognised - fixed and mutation-tested. check-rls-policies.mjs now detects the WITH CHECK (true) shape too, with its own baseline (20260827090000) so the historical backlog is listed rather than failing. REMAINING: 58 open policies. Most of the SELECT ones are deliberate (marketing content, SEO, public pseo pages) and several INSERT ones are genuine public-write endpoints - lead capture, demo requests, unsubscribe, calculator sessions - which must NOT be closed blindly. The ones still worth triage are security_events, security_alerts, ai_lead_scores, task_activity_logs, conversion_events, knowledge_base_views and the companies-creation policies, each of which has a live client write that needs converting first. CORRECTION during the same change: rate_limit_violations was in the first draft of the deny list and had to come out. _shared/rate-limiter.ts writes it with whatever client checkRateLimit is handed, and most callers pass a user-JWT one, so denying it would have stopped violations being recorded - and since checkRateLimit computes `allowed` by counting those rows, the limit would have stopped tripping altogether. A silent loss of rate limiting, not of logging. check-rls-write-paths.mjs did not catch it because it only scanned supabase/functions/*/index.ts and skipped _shared/ entirely; it now scans _shared too and reports caller-supplied clients separately, as sites to audit by hand rather than as failures. Verified by putting rate_limit_violations back in the watch list and confirming the guard names rate-limiter.ts line 101.

userStories.title: No rate limit in the system has ever blocked a request
userStories.description: As anyone with a script, I can call every rate-limited endpoint as fast as I like. supabase/functions/_shared/rate-limiter.ts checkRateLimit() decides allowed by counting rows in rate_limit_violations for the identifier and endpoint inside the window, and inserts a row into that table only when the request is NOT allowed. From an empty table the count is 0, so allowed is true, so no row is inserted, so the count stays 0. It cannot bootstrap. Nothing else writes the table - dos-protection references it three times and all three are selects. enforceRateLimit(), added later, delegates straight to checkRateLimit, so it inherits the same behaviour. That means all 14 functions scripts/check-rate-limit-coverage.mjs reports as enforcing a limit are calling a function that always returns allowed: true, including signup-with-otp, send-auth-otp, verify-auth-otp, verify-mfa-login and the AI endpoints that spend money per call. The table rate_limit_state exists for exactly this purpose - identifier, endpoint, request_count, window_start, is_blocked, blocked_until - and is written by nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: A request beyond the configured limit is refused, demonstrated by a test that drives requests through the real module from an empty store rather than from pre-seeded rows
The counter is incremented atomically, so two concurrent requests cannot both read the same count and both pass
Every checkRateLimit call site passes a client that can actually write the counter
The existing src/lib/__tests__/rateLimiter.test.ts stops re-implementing the logic, or is replaced by one that imports it
Failing open on a database error stays deliberate and documented, rather than becoming the only behaviour
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-08-27 while excluding rate_limit_violations from the US-306 deny list - I needed to know who wrote that table and why, and the answer was that the only writer is unreachable. Proven, not reasoned: supabase/functions/_shared/rate-limiter.test.ts drives 50 requests against a limit of 3 through the real checkRateLimit with a fake client that behaves like the table (what you insert is what you read back). Zero blocked, zero rows written, requestCount still 0 on the fiftieth. A fourth case seeds the rows the limiter is waiting for and shows it does block - the arithmetic was never the problem. Why it was never noticed: src/lib/__tests__/rateLimiter.test.ts RE-IMPLEMENTS the logic rather than importing it, and hands the copy a mock pre-seeded with violation rows. So it proves the arithmetic and never asks how a row gets into the table. It has 20-odd passing cases and could not have caught this. That is the lesson worth keeping - a test that reconstructs its subject tests the reconstruction. Fix direction: an atomic SECURITY DEFINER RPC over rate_limit_state (pg_advisory_xact_lock on identifier+endpoint, then read-modify-write) rather than select-then-update in the edge function, which is racy. Note the call sites first: of ~19 checkRateLimit callers, only some pass a service-role client, and rate_limit_state is now service-role-only per US-306. FIXED 2026-08-27 the same day. Migration 20260827100000 adds public.consume_rate_limit(p_identifier, p_endpoint, p_max_requests, p_window_minutes) RETURNS TABLE (allowed, request_count, retry_after): SECURITY DEFINER with search_path = '', taking pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(identifier || ':' || endpoint, 0)) before the read-modify-write so two concurrent requests cannot both read the same count and both pass - which is the specific failure a rate limiter exists to prevent. The lock avoids needing a unique index on rate_limit_state, so no lock is taken on a pre-existing table and the CONCURRENTLY question does not arise. Semantics: the count includes the request being decided, so at maxRequests 3 requests 1-3 pass and the 4th does not. EXECUTE is revoked from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated and granted to service_role alone, because a function any client could call would let one caller burn another caller's quota by passing their IP. checkRateLimit now calls that RPC and still fails open on a database error, deliberately - but loudly, since failing open silently is what let this sit. Three callers passed a user-JWT client and were converted to createServiceClient(): setup-mfa, data-subject-delete (x2), data-subject-export (x2). scripts/check-rate-limit-coverage.mjs now also fails when any checkRateLimit/enforceRateLimit call is handed a non-service client, resolved on the TypeScript AST in two passes so a service key held in a variable (const key = Deno.env.get(...); createClient(url, key)) is recognised - the first regex version false-positived on ai-estimating, analyze-support-ticket and email-unsubscribe, all of which were correct. Mutation-tested with both a user-JWT client and an anon-key client. src/lib/__tests__/rateLimiter.test.ts no longer re-implements the module; its real cases moved to supabase/functions/_shared/rate-limiter.test.ts (21 tests, importing the module), and what remains is a guard against the copy coming back. consume_rate_limit also logs the refusal to rate_limit_violations, so dos-protection's attack statistics keep working and that table now holds only what its name says - nothing reads it to make a decision any more, which is exactly what was wrong before. Writing that insert turned up one more confirmation the old path was dead: it named limit_value and window_minutes, neither of which is a column, passed a bare identifier into ip_address (INET), and omitted identifier_type, method, limit_exceeded_by, time_window_seconds and action_taken, all NOT NULL. Even on the branch it could never reach, it would have errored. The new insert casts to inet only when the identifier looks like an address, since a user id is not one and a failed cast would abort the call and take the limiter down with it.

userStories.title: Two test files hung the unit suite forever on infinite render loops
userStories.description: As anyone waiting on CI, I want npm run test:run to finish. src/components/accessibility/__tests__/AccessibleForm.a11y.test.tsx and src/pages/__tests__/Settings.a11y.test.tsx never completed - a 90s timeout killed each, and left unbounded a vitest worker reached 4.7 GB RSS and the suite reported two Worker exited unexpectedly errors. US-213 makes Unit Tests a required merge check, so a suite that cannot finish blocks every merge. Both were the same failure: a useEffect whose dependency is an object recreated on every render, so the effect re-runs, sets state, re-renders, and produces another fresh object. React does not raise Maximum update depth for this shape because each iteration is scheduled in its own task rather than nested synchronously in one commit, so it spins rather than erroring.
acceptanceCriteria: Both files complete, and npm run test:run finishes without a worker being killed
AccessibleForm no longer re-runs its error-sync effect on every render
The Settings auth mock returns a stable object, matching the real AuthContext which memoises its value
The Settings page effect keys on identifying primitives rather than whole objects, since it navigates and toasts
The Settings tests exercise the page rather than its redirect
userStories.notes: FOUND 2026-08-27 by timing all 110 test files individually after a full run took 1490s with two worker crashes; exactly two files timed out. AccessibleForm.tsx had initialErrors = {} as a DEFAULT PARAMETER and useEffect(() => setErrors(initialErrors), [initialErrors]) - every caller who omits the prop gets a fresh object each render, so the dependency never compares equal. Bisected to the exact combination with a probe: form alone passes, form with a field and a pinned initialErrors passes, form with a field and the default hangs. Fixed by comparing serialized content with a ref guard so the mount does not re-set what useState already seeded. registerField/unregisterField also built a new Set unconditionally; they now return prev when nothing changed - not the loop itself, but fuel for it. Settings.a11y.test.tsx mocked useAuth with inline object literals, so every render produced fresh user and userProfile, and the page effect (which calls navigate and toast) re-fired forever. The real AuthContext memoises its value at AuthContext.tsx:1202, so the mock was modelling something that cannot happen. Hoisted the objects, and changed role from admin to root_admin - src/pages/admin/Settings.tsx is root_admin-only, so every test in that file had been exercising the redirect rather than the page it claims to test. Also narrowed the page effect to [user?.id, userProfile?.role, loading, navigate]: an effect with side effects that keys on object identity re-fires for free the moment any caller hands it a fresh reference. 22 tests pass in AccessibleForm, 4 in Settings, both previously infinite.
